meta.description: Programme milestones and robotic/crewed missions relevant to the lunar south pole, with status as of 2026-11-14 as recorded in the research notes.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive; lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). null = not published / not in notes.
notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated. All PLANNED dates are provisional.
status vocabulary: FLOWN, PLANNED, SUPERSEDED (an older plan since changed), CANCELLED, OPERATING, LOST.
'secondary_source': true means the row rests wholly or mainly on Wikipedia, tracker sites, trade press or search-result excerpts rather than agency primary pages.
Item 'type' values: crewed_mission, lander_system, programme_milestone, programme, robotic_flown, robotic_planned, orbiter, relay_system, surface_element.
Conflicting values between notes (dates, coordinates, distances) are kept side by side.
No landing coordinates have been published for Blue Moon MK1 'Endurance', Griffin-1, VIPER (2027 delivery), IM-4, IM-5, PROMISE or Chang'e-8.

items.name: Artemis I
items.outcome: success

items.name: Artemis II
items.dates: Launch 1 Apr 2026 22:35:12 UTC; splashdown 10 Apr 2026 8:07 pm ET (11 Apr 00:07 UTC) off San Diego
items.profile: Crewed free-return lunar flyby; Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen; Orion 'Integrity'; 695,081 miles; reentry 24,664 mph
items.outcome: success

items.name: Artemis III
items.dates: 2027: NASA says 'next year' (Oct 2026); 'mid-2027' still official per SpacePolicyOnline; Ars Technica via Wikipedia 'no earlier than late 2027'; Wikipedia infobox NET June 2027; reported ~90 days behind (Sep 2026)
items.profile: Crewed LEO test, 14-17 days: Orion (SLS Block 1, LC-39B, ~230 nmi / 430 km circular, 33 deg) docks on Day 3 with Blue Moon MK2 test vehicle (crew inside ~2 days), then on Day 8 with a Starship test article for ~2 hours, no crew transfer. Crew: Randy Bresnik (CDR), Luca Parmitano (ESA, PLT), Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas; backup Bob Hines. Blue Moon test vehicle loiter: up to 30 days (SpacePolicyOnline) or up to 90 days (Wikipedia).
items.superseded_plan: First crewed south-polar landing with Starship HLS from NRHO, ~6.5-day stay (SUPERSEDED)
items.lessons: Re-plan followed an Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel warning that Artemis III was trying to do too much at once.
items.caveat: 'mid-2027' vs 'late 2027' unresolved; no NASA statement dated Nov 2026 with a specific date.

items.name: Artemis IV
items.dates: 2028 ('early 2028' in Feb/Mar 2026 reporting; trackers changed to just '2028' between 25 Oct and 1 Nov 2026; NASA goal landing attempt by end of 2028)
items.profile: 4 crew on Orion/SLS; 2 land near the South Pole with Starship HLS or Blue Moon MK2 (lander chosen by readiness; Plan A Starship, Plan B New Glenn + Mark 2); stay 'several days'; two moonwalks of about two hours each; lighter 'sortie' suit

landing.intended_site: near the lunar South Pole; no region named; site undecided as of Oct-Nov 2026

items.lessons: NASA (23 Oct 2026): more data needed from robotic landers before a final site decision. Stated concerns: steep slopes, low Sun angles, temperature extremes, fewer abort options. A tracker says the nine 2024 regions carry over to Artemis IV (secondary, not a NASA statement); NASA's LPSC 2026 abstract says the nine do not constrain Artemis IV. An Artemis IV landing-site workshop was held 10 Sep 2025 to define figures of merit. One newsletter (1 June 2026) reports NASA was considering a first landing away from the south pole (secondary, unconfirmed); a NASEM report (Oct 2026) identified four non-polar sites.
items.caveat: No landing coordinates; crew, stay length in days and SLS upper stage not confirmed by a primary source. Upper-stage conflict: Wikipedia 'Artemis IV' says final SLS flight with ICPS; Wikipedia 'Artemis program' says Centaur V replaces ICPS starting with Artemis IV.

items.name: Artemis V
items.profile: Same standardized SLS; start of base build-up

items.name: Starship HLS
items.dates: Contract $2.89B (Apr 2021), option exercised Mar 2022, contract growth 6%; first in-orbit propellant transfer attempt early 2027; uncrewed lunar landing test late 2027; Starship reached orbit on its first uncrewed orbital flight in Sep 2026
items.profile: 2028 architecture: tankers fill a depot in LEO, depot fuels the lander; lander docks with Orion in Earth orbit and performs TLI, pushing Orion to low lunar orbit; two crew descend, stay 'several days'. Original assignment Artemis III and IV (SUPERSEDED); now no fixed assignment.
items.lessons: OIG IG-26-004 (10 Mar 2026): at least two years of delay since 2021; propellant transfer test slipped Mar 2025 -> Mar 2026; tip-over risk flagged because of vehicle height. ASAP (22 Oct 2026): only one uncrewed landing test per provider; first use of cryogenic propellants on the Moon.

items.name: Blue Moon Mark 2
items.dates: Contract $3.4B (May 2023), growth under 1%; New Glenn not returned to flight after the May 2026 pad explosion as of early Nov 2026 (return possible by late 2026)
items.profile: 2028 architecture: propellant transfer deferred; three transfer stages built from MK1/MK2 hardware act as a multistage tug; stack goes to an elliptical polar lunar orbit where it meets Orion (Wikipedia: perilune 100 km, apolune 6,500 km, coplanar apsides); two crew descend to the South Pole. Original assignment Artemis V (SUPERSEDED).
items.lessons: OIG: at least eight months behind, further 11-month slip expected; 2024 PDR shortfalls open; manual-control decisions open.
items.caveat: Orbit numbers (100 x 6,500 km) are from Wikipedia only; NASA published no altitudes/periods.

items.name: FY2026 budget proposal to end SLS/Orion after Artemis III; reversed by One Big Beautiful Bill Act
items.outcome: SLS and Orion funded beyond Artemis III

items.name: First-landing contract opened to competition (acting administrator Sean Duffy)
items.outcome: cited Starship HLS timeline concerns

items.name: Jared Isaacman sworn in as NASA administrator
items.outcome: Artemis III then still first landing (SUPERSEDED)

items.name: Artemis re-plan: Artemis III becomes LEO demonstration; Artemis IV first crewed landing
items.dates: 27 Feb 2026 (KSC briefing; posted on X 3 Mar 2026)
items.outcome: SLS Block 1B and Block 2 cancelled (standardize on Block 1; EUS and Mobile Launcher 2 not used); NRHO later dropped

items.name: NASA OIG report on HLS contracts (IG-26-004)
items.outcome: Nearly $7B obligated, over $18B projected through FY2030; NASA has no capability to rescue astronauts stranded in space or on the surface
items.caveat: Full report text not retrieved; press summary and news coverage only.

items.name: 'Ignition' event: Gateway paused; Moon Base plan announced
items.outcome: Gateway 'paused in its current form', hardware repurposed for surface operations; Orion crews transfer directly to landers. Conflict: Wikipedia lists Gateway as 'cancelled'; NASA wording 'paused'; another note: 'not formally cancelled in the sources found'.

items.name: ICPS not used on Artemis III (kept for Artemis IV); non-propulsive spacer flown
New Glenn exploded on the pad days after the 26 May Moon Base briefing
items.outcome: Schedule concerns for Artemis III and fall-2026 CLPS missions
items.caveat: Conflict between notes: the water-ice note calls the pad-explosion claim unverified (low-reliability aggregator https://spaceodysseyhub.com/moon/landers/blue-moon-mk1-viper); the programme note cites Astronomy.com and a CRS In Focus report.

items.name: Artemis III hardware: booster stacking complete (30 Sep 2026, VAB High Bay 3); core stage mated (28 Oct 2026)
items.outcome: All four RS-25s installed; tanking test at Pad 39B 'in the coming months'; adapters ship to KSC early 2027

items.name: ASAP concerns on lander readiness
items.outcome: Only one uncrewed landing test per provider; first use of cryogenic propellants on the Moon

items.name: NASA briefing and web feature confirming 2027 LEO test and 2028 landings; NRHO replaced
items.outcome: 'Neither provider is assigned to a specific lunar landing mission'; rendezvous in low lunar orbit (Starship) or elliptical polar orbit (Blue Moon); NRHO SUPERSEDED

items.name: CLPS 2.0 providers selected; PROMISE delivery awarded
items.outcome: CLPS 2.0 = 10-year IDIQ, $10B combined, eight providers (Blue Origin, Firefly, Intuitive Machines, ispace-U.S., Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, SpaceX, Voyager Technologies)

items.name: Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS)
items.dates: CLPS 1.0: 14 missions to five vendors, four launched; four more landings awarded 30 Jun 2026 for late 2028
items.outcome: 2024 OIG: average delays of 14 months; CLPS 1.0 ceiling raised to $4.2B from $2.6B

items.name: Moon Base Phase 1 'Experiment, Learn'
items.profile: Robotic and early uncrewed missions to scout and prepare ahead of astronaut missions in 2028; rovers; MoonFall hopper drones; relay and observation satellites; early power, navigation, communication and nuclear RHU demos. Up to 25 missions including 21 landings; 4 tons of payload.
items.caveat: Secondary reporting differs: Phase 1 'through 2028', 25 launches, 21 landings, over 4,000 kg (https://starlust.org/nasa-has-adopted-a-3-phase-approach-to-establish-a-moon-base-heres-what-it-looks-like/).

items.name: Moon Base Phase 2 'Early Habitation'
items.profile: Semi-permanent infrastructure; improved solar and RTG-based power; upgraded rovers; surface-to-orbit communications across the South Pole; about 60 tons of cargo in 24 landings. Begins once initial sites are confirmed; infrastructure 'across multiple locations'; crewed visits rise from one to two per year.
items.caveat: Secondary: 27 launches, 24 landings, over 60,000 kg.

items.name: Moon Base Phase 3 'Sustained Human Presence'
items.profile: Semi-permanent habitation modules; operational fission surface power station; pressurized rovers; logistics network; up to 38 tons of cargo per year.
items.caveat: Secondary: 29 launches, 28 landings, over 150,000 kg cumulative, more than $10B. Cost conflict: 'approximately $20 billion over the next seven years' (Isaacman, 24 Mar 2026, https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nasa-moon-base-plan-lunar-south-pole/) vs '$30 billion' over a decade (https://www.astronomy.com/space-exploration/how-nasa-plans-to-build-a-moon-base/).

items.outcome: Deliberate impact; mass spectrometer detected water during descent
items.caveat: No coordinates in notes.

items.name: Lunar Prospector end-of-mission impact
items.outcome: Deliberate crash; no detectable water vapour plume
items.caveat: No impact coordinates in notes.

items.name: LCROSS
items.outcome: Impact; water 5.6 +/- 2.9 wt% in ejecta ('nearly 5% water' in one secondary summary)
items.lessons: Only ground-truth volatile detection at the south pole; see psr_and_ice.json.

items.name: Luna-25

landing.site: Crashed on SW rim of Pontecoulant G; new crater about 10 m; about 400 km from target

items.outcome: Failure after an orbit-lowering burn
items.lessons: Lost during a pre-landing orbit burn, i.e. before any polar-terrain effect.

items.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram lander, Pragyan rover)

landing.site: Statio Shiv Shakti, between Manzinus C and Simpelius N

items.outcome: Success; first soft landing near the south pole; lander and rover worked one lunar day (rover 12 days); no response to wake-up calls 22 Sep 2023
items.lessons: Landing zone ~16 km2 chosen from Chandrayaan-2 orbiter imagery; hover ~30 s at ~150 m to pick a clear spot; fixes vs Chandrayaan-2: attitude authority 25 deg/s vs 10 deg/s, laser Doppler velocimetry, stronger legs, more redundancy; landed about a day after local dawn; ChaSTE: 355 K on 6-deg sun-facing slope vs ~332 K on flat ground 1 m away; exhaust removed about 3 cm of regolith.

items.name: IM-1 Odysseus
items.dates: Landed 22 Feb 2024, 23:23:53 UTC; power lost 29 Feb (ended 28/29 Feb, sources differ)

landing.site: Near Malapert A, about 300 km from the pole; elevation 2,579 m

items.outcome: Partial: landed within about 1.5 km of target (100 m precision goal missed), on a 12 deg slope in a degraded ~1 km crater, broke a leg, rested ~30 deg tilted; about seven days of data; not revived after the night
items.lessons: Laser rangefinders unusable because a physical safety switch was not enabled before launch; NASA Navigation Doppler Lidar patched in hours before landing; came in fast, a leg caught and it tipped; antennas mis-pointed so data rates far below plan.
items.caveat: Coordinates come from secondary sources / search excerpts per the programme note. Intended target coordinates not in notes.

items.name: IM-2 Athena (PRIME-1: TRIDENT drill + MSolo)
items.dates: Launched 26 Feb 2025; lunar orbit 3 Mar; landed 6 Mar 2025 (17:28 UTC per NASA slides; ~17:28 per LROC note; 17:31 UTC per collectSPACE); operations ended 7 Mar 06:15

landing.miss_distance: about 250 m (LROC/collectSPACE); ~500 m per NASA slides; ~400 m per press
landing.distance_from_pole: 160 km (LROC, intended site); ~158 km (derived by researcher)

items.outcome: Failure: on its side in a shadowed crater about 20 m wide at about -173 C (~100 K); ~100 W; operations ended <13 h after landing (~12 h); >400 MB returned; southernmost landing to date
items.lessons: Rangefinder returned optical noise even when the laser was not firing; three orbits of troubleshooting failed; waiting longer would have moved the site outside onboard crater maps; touchdown at 10-13 m/s while software believed it was ~400 m up; arrays not facing the Sun and dust-coated. MSolo spectra dominated by Earth air/propellant -> bake-out needed.

items.name: Lunar Trailblazer
items.dates: Launched 26 Feb 2025; contact lost one day after launch; mission ended 31 Jul 2025
items.outcome: No water maps produced

items.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
items.outcome: Success; only CLPS 1.0 mission to fully meet objectives; operated > 14 days
items.lessons: Ran on batteries ~5 hours through the 14 Mar 2025 total lunar eclipse; reported surface temperature fall from about +40 C to -170 C; worked ~5 h into the night.
items.caveat: Not polar; coordinates not in notes.

items.name: Peregrine Mission One
items.outcome: Failure: propellant leak, no landing attempt

items.name: Danuri / KPLO with NASA ShadowCam
items.dates: In orbit since Dec 2022; extended to end of 2027
items.outcome: Orbit lowered from 100 km to 60 km for seven months; ShadowCam PDS releases Feb and Jun 2026

landing.site: Mare Serenitatis (from researcher's memory; not re-verified); not polar

items.name: Moon Base I = Blue Moon Pathfinder Mission 1 (Blue Moon MK1 'Endurance', MK1-101)
items.dates: NET Q1 2027 (launch-listing sites/Wikipedia); a June 2026 newsletter: no earlier than 2H 2027; was NET fall 2026 / end-2026 (SUPERSEDED)
items.lessons: Privately funded; NASA payloads SCALPSS (four plume cameras) and LRA (eight retroreflectors); precision landing within 100 m; thermal-vacuum test at JSC done; cryogenic loading next (Aug 2026). Would be among the first landing attempts poleward of 85 S.
items.caveat: Landing coordinates not published. Conflicting dates kept (Q1 2027 vs NET 2H 2027).

items.name: Moon Base II = Griffin Mission One
items.agency: Astrobotic (acquired by Voyager Technologies, Jun 2026), Falcon Heavy; NASA CLPS
items.dates: Listing moved from 31 Dec 2026 to 31 Jan 2027 (seen 1 Nov 2026); NASA in Aug 2026 said 'late 2026'; NET Jul 2026 SUPERSEDED
items.lessons: Over 1,100 lb cargo; Astrolab FLIP rover with five NASA payloads; informs LTV; METAL He-3 measurement payload.
items.caveat: Landing coordinates not published.

items.name: Moon Base III = IM-3 (Nova-C 'Trinity'; Lunar Vertex)
items.lessons: Changes after IM-1/IM-2: primary and redundant rangefinders from two vendors covering 15 km to 5 km and terminal descent; airplane/helicopter sensor tests; larger crater-map library; 12 lunar orbits before landing; review of ground-contact conditions, stability, landing-gear durability. First Khon relay satellite planned to launch with IM-3.

items.name: VIPER (CS-7, Blue Moon Pathfinder Mission 2)
items.agency: NASA; delivery Blue Origin Blue Moon MK1
items.status: PLANNED (cancelled 17 Jul 2024, SUPERSEDED; revived by CLPS task order Sep 2025, up to ~$190M)
items.dates: Late 2027 / fall 2027; a June 2026 newsletter judges 2H 2028 more likely. Original plan: landing Nov 2023, then Nov 2024.

landing.intended_site: Mons Mouton, western edge of Nobile

items.lessons: Contingent on first MK1 landing; 100-day mission in south-polar summer; TRIDENT 1 m drill, NSS, NIRVSS, MSolo; slipping past Nov 2025 in the original plan would have meant waiting 9-12 months for suitable lighting.
items.caveat: Task-order date given as 19 Sep 2025 in one note and 'Sept 2025' elsewhere. 2021 coordinates may be superseded for the 2027 delivery; updated landing coordinates not published.

items.agency: NASA; delivery Blue Origin ($188M plus $280.4M option, two MK1-derived landers)

items.lessons: About 1 t each; deploy about 2 km from crewed landing sites; up to 400 km total driving.

items.name: Chang'e-7 (orbiter, lander, rover, hopper)
items.status: PLANNED (2026 launch and Nov 2026 landing SUPERSEDED)
items.dates: Launch scrubbed 23 Aug 2026 (NOTAM window opened 24 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC, daily 00:00-04:00 UTC to 31 Aug); 'cannot take place during the planned window this year'; now 2027 at the earliest
items.lessons: Launch date constrained by the need to land in the best lighting at Shackleton, so missing the August 2026 window pushed the mission to 2027. Landing accuracy better than 100 m; hopper with water-molecule analyser into a PSR; relay Queqiao-2.
items.caveat: Target coordinates are unofficial, from secondary sources; no CNSA primary page read. One note (science) found no report of the delay and still lists 2H 2026; the programme and timing notes record the Aug 2026 scrub.

items.name: Chang'e-8 (ISRU demo)
items.dates: Around 2029 (Sep 2024 plan said 2028); SpaceNews (Sep 2026): programme may be reconfigured

landing.intended_site: Leibnitz Beta plateau (Mons Mouton); earlier candidates Amundsen, Cabeus, Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge

items.caveat: Coordinates not published.

items.name: ILRS (China/Russia)
items.dates: Construction from 2031 (Scientific American); basic robotic operations by 2030 (tracker); Chinese crewed landing by 2030

items.name: NASA Near Space Network lunar relay (NSN 2.2) / Intuitive Machines 'Khon' constellation
items.dates: IDIQ max $4.82B; base period 1 Oct 2024 - 30 Sep 2029, option to 30 Sep 2034; first relay to launch with IM-3, two more with IM-4 (2027), remainder on a fifth mission
items.outcome: Five-satellite comm/nav constellation for the South Pole region; NASA: without relays 'landing opportunities at the Moon's South Pole will be significantly limited'
items.caveat: Schedule from 2024 trade press; may be out of date. Whether any relay is in orbit as of Nov 2026 not confirmed.

items.name: ESA Moonlight; precursor Lunar Pathfinder (SSTL)
items.dates: Initial services end of 2028, full operations 2030; Lunar Pathfinder to begin operations 2026 (status unconfirmed)
items.outcome: 5 satellites (4 navigation, 1 communications), 3 ground stations, prioritising south-pole coverage. Lunar Pathfinder orbit: perilune altitude 673.4 km, apolune 7,331.8 km, inclination 46.8 deg, period 10 h
items.caveat: Lunar Pathfinder orbit from 2023 slides via search excerpt.

items.name: Queqiao-2
items.outcome: Elliptical frozen orbit planned ~200 x 16,000 km, 24 h period, 62.4 deg inclination (observed ~254 x 16,941 km, 26.18 h, 119.25 deg retrograde per amateur tracking); 4.2 m X-band antenna; supports Chang'e 6, 7, 8; a 12 h orbit planned for later south-polar missions (~8 h contact per orbit)
